defect: Crude Define-phase defect (PLAN §9): the problem statement embeds the fix ('...so we need to buy a second espresso machine') and cause language ('because we only have one machine'), and the SMART goal is written as the same solution ('Install a second espresso machine...') rather than a measurable target outcome. Both fields are otherwise complete (what/where/when/magnitude all present; the goal carries a metric, baseline, target, unit, date, and a guardrail metric) so the ONLY thing wrong is that the student wrote the fix where the effect belongs -- the textbook 'solution-shaped problem statement' PLAN §9 names by name.

deterministic_layer.notes: Prescore's problem_statement_solution_language and goal_solution_language keyword heuristics both fire correctly (they catch 'because' and 'install' -- prescore/charter.py's SOLUTION_LANGUAGE_KEYWORDS). What prescore CANNOT do is grade whether the fix has been proven appropriate to the (still-unverified) cause, whether the goal is sized to the problem's magnitude, or write the concrete rewrite a student needs -- that judgment is the review mode's job, using these two flags as its starting checklist (PLAN §5.1: 'the model's job is judgment on top of the checklist, not rediscovering it').

prescore_flags.detail: at least one guardrail metric named

must_catch: R-DEF-02 (problem statement quality) should verdict needs_work: the statement embeds the fix ('buy a second espresso machine') and cause language ('because') instead of stating only what/where/when/magnitude.

R-DEF-03 (goal and metrics) should verdict needs_work: the goal statement itself is the prescribed fix ('Install a second espresso machine...') rather than a measurable target outcome -- SMART in mechanical shape (metric/baseline/target/date all present) but not in substance.
schema_note: Nothing here is schema-blocked. CharterArtifact.problem_statement and .goal are free-text fields with no content-quality validator at the schema layer (charter.py's own docstring: solution-shaped language is a prescore flag, never a rejection, per PLAN §4.2's hard/soft split) -- this fixture needed no compromise to reach its strongest form.
